name: mainstream_persistence
evidence: Parent-child correlation in completed family size is repeatedly estimated near 0.1-0.2 (Murphy 1999; Murphy and Knudsen 2002); twin studies put the genetic component of fertility variation near 0.2 (Kohler et al. 1999, 2002).
provenance: Assistant's recollection of the published literature. NOT fetched from a source file. Verify against the papers before any publication.
notes: Spec 6.2: this is intergenerational fertility PERSISTENCE, the combined genetic plus cultural channel, not heritability. Heritability is the genetic part alone.

name: mainstream_propensity_cv
evidence: Dispersion of children ever born in completed low-fertility cohorts: a mean near 1.8-2.0 with a standard deviation near 1.1-1.3 implies a coefficient of variation near 0.6.
provenance: Assistant's recollection of the published literature. NOT fetched. The Human Fertility Database would settle this properly and is not yet ingested.
notes: Sets how far apart the latent low, middle and high propensity types are. Larger values give selection more to work with.

name: mainstream_types
evidence: None. A structural choice, not an estimate.
notes: Three latent fertility-propensity types with no ethnic, religious or political label attached.

name: group_retention_haredi
evidence: Studies of leaving Haredi communities in Israel generally find that roughly 10-15% of those raised in them do not remain, though definitions of leaving differ widely.
provenance: Assistant's recollection. NOT fetched. Definitions vary enough that the range matters more than the central value.
notes: Spec 6.6: retention is as consequential as fertility itself.

name: group_fertility_haredi
evidence: Israel CBS reports Haredi total fertility near 6.4-6.6, and falling slowly over the last decade.
notes: Recorded as a level, converted to a propensity relative to the country's own fertility at run time.

name: group_share_haredi
evidence: Israel CBS estimates the Haredi population near 13-14% of Israel's population in the mid-2020s.

name: group_retention_amish
evidence: Retention among Old Order Amish is generally reported near 85-90% in recent cohorts, having risen substantially over the twentieth century (Kraybill and colleagues).
notes: The historical rise is itself evidence that retention is not a constant of nature.

name: group_fertility_amish
evidence: Old Order Amish completed family size is generally reported between five and seven, declining slowly.

name: group_share_amish
evidence: Roughly 400,000 Amish in a United States population near 340 million.
provenance: Assistant's recollection of Young Center population estimates. NOT fetched.
notes: Applied to the United States only.

name: defector_high_propensity_weight
provenance: Scenario knob. Spec 6.5 argues defectors should keep part of the fertility profile for a generation or two; how much is not established.
notes: Share of children leaving a named group who land in the mainstream HIGH propensity type rather than being spread across the mainstream distribution.

name: development_decline_per_decade
evidence: None. This is the quantity the project is trying to learn, not one it can look up.
provenance: Scenario knob, and the most important one in the model. Spec 6.9 requires it be a stated path rather than a fitted trend.
notes: How much the fertility ENVIRONMENT falls per decade under continued development pressure: what a person of fixed propensity has, not what the population has.

name: development_floor
notes: Floor on the environment multiplier relative to 2024, so continued development pressure cannot drive the environment to zero.

name: group_convergence_per_generation
evidence: Group fertility differentials have narrowed in several documented cases, but no general rate is established.
provenance: Scenario knob. Spec 6.7 forbids extrapolating a small group's present behaviour unchanged after it becomes a large share of society.
notes: How much a named group's fertility advantage decays per generation under the convergence scenario.
